title: Crowds Flock to Taipei Zoo's First-Ever Penguin Parade
summaryZh: 北市動物園首辦企鵝散步，43隻非洲企鵝出巡，人潮爆滿。
summaryHi: ताइपे चिड़ियाघर की पहली पेंगुइन परेड में उम्मीद से कहीं ज़्यादा लोग पहुँचे।
summaryEs: El primer desfile de pingüinos del zoo de Taipéi atrae a muchas más personas de lo esperado.
summaryJa: 台北市立動物園で初のペンギン散歩、43羽が行進し予想以上の人出。
summaryKo: 타이베이 동물원 첫 펭귄 퍼레이드에 예상보다 훨씬 많은 인파.
summaryEn: Taipei Zoo's first penguin parade, with 43 African penguins, drew far bigger crowds than expected.
paragraphs: Taipei Zoo's first-ever "penguin parade" proved far more popular than anticipated on Thursday, with crowds gathering long before the birds emerged.

In the 15-minute trial event, 43 African penguins were allowed out of their enclosure to waddle along a set route in front of spectators. It began at 9:30 in the morning and was accompanied by a talk from zookeepers.

Social media users reported that some people had turned up by 8 a.m., and that by 9 a.m., the queue extended from the zoo's entrance to the Maokong Gondola station. The zoo described the turnout as larger than expected.
Beyond entertaining visitors, the walk has a health purpose. Regular exercise reduces the risk of bumblefoot, an infection of the feet that can develop when penguins do not move enough.

The concept was borrowed from Asahiyama Zoo in Hokkaido, where king penguins march across the snow. Taipei's version will only take place when temperatures are below 24°C. Given the limited space, the zoo is considering numbered tickets or holding walks on days when the Penguin House is closed, and it has asked visitors not to chase, touch or feed the birds or use selfie sticks.
Taipei Zoo did something new on Thursday. Its penguins went for a walk outside!
Forty-three African penguins left their home. They walked on a path in front of visitors. The walk started at 9:30 in the morning and lasted 15 minutes.
Many more people came than the zoo expected. Some people arrived at 8 o'clock. By 9 o'clock, the line was very long.
Why do penguins need to walk? Walking is good exercise. Without exercise, penguins can get sore feet.
The idea comes from a zoo in Japan. Visitors must be quiet. They must not touch or feed the penguins. The zoo may give out tickets next time.

paragraphs: Taipei Zoo held its first-ever "penguin parade" on Thursday, November 19, and far more visitors came than expected.

During the event, 43 African penguins left their enclosure and walked along a fixed route while people watched. The parade began at 9:30 a.m., lasted 15 minutes and included a short talk by zookeepers.
According to posts on social media, some visitors arrived as early as 8 a.m. By 9 a.m., the queue stretched all the way from the zoo entrance to the Maokong Gondola station.
The zoo explained that the walk is not only for fun. It gives the birds exercise and helps prevent bumblefoot, a painful foot problem caused by too little movement.

The idea came from Asahiyama Zoo in Hokkaido, Japan, where king penguins walk on snow. In Taipei, walks only happen when it is cooler than 24°C. Because space is limited, the zoo may use numbered tickets in future, and visitors are asked to stay quiet and not touch or feed the birds.

它能讓企鵝運動，並預防趾瘤症——一種因活動太少而引起的腳部疼痛問題。
這個點子來自日本北海道的旭山動物園，那裡的國王企鵝會在雪地上散步。

由於空間有限，動物園未來可能發號碼牌，並請遊客保持安靜、不要觸摸或餵食企鵝。

paragraphs: Taipei Zoo's inaugural "penguin parade" drew crowds that far exceeded expectations on Thursday, offering a glimpse of how popular the experiment could become.

During the 15-minute trial, 43 African penguins were released from their enclosure to waddle along a designated route before an audience, while zookeepers delivered a short commentary. The event, which began at 9:30 a.m., was intended partly to gauge how visitors would respond.

Judging by accounts posted on Threads, the answer was unequivocal: some enthusiasts had arrived by 8 a.m., and within an hour the queue snaked from the main entrance all the way to the Maokong Gondola station.
The outing is more than a spectacle. According to the zoo, it provides exercise that lowers the risk of bumblefoot, a foot condition associated with prolonged inactivity in captive birds.

The initiative draws inspiration from Asahiyama Zoo in Hokkaido, where king penguins parade across the snow; Taipei's warmer climate means walks will be held only when temperatures fall below 24°C. Given the limited space, organisers are weighing numbered tickets or scheduling walks on days the Penguin House is closed, and have urged spectators to avoid noise, sudden movements and selfie sticks.
sentZh: 台北市立動物園首屆「企鵝遊行」週四吸引的人潮遠超預期，讓人一窺這項實驗可能有多受歡迎。
在這場 15 分鐘的試辦中，43 隻非洲企鵝被放出展區，在觀眾面前沿著指定路線搖擺前進，同時由保育員進行簡短解說。
這場上午 9 點 30 分開始的活動，部分目的在於了解遊客的反應。
從 Threads 上的貼文來看，答案再明確不過：有些愛好者早上 8 點就到了，不到一小時，隊伍便從大門口一路蜿蜒到貓空纜車站。
這次外出不只是一場奇觀。
據動物園表示，散步提供的運動能降低趾瘤症的風險，這種腳部疾病與圈養鳥類長期缺乏活動有關。
這項計畫的靈感來自北海道的旭山動物園，那裡的國王企鵝會在雪地上遊行；而台北氣候較溫暖，因此只會在氣溫低於攝氏 24 度時舉行。
由於空間有限，主辦單位正在權衡發放號碼牌，或改在企鵝館休館日安排散步，並呼籲觀眾避免喧嘩、突然的動作和自拍棒。

paragraphs: An experimental "penguin parade" at Taipei Zoo attracted an unexpectedly large audience on Thursday, underlining the public's appetite for close encounters with wildlife.

In the inaugural 15-minute session, 43 African penguins were permitted to leave their enclosure and proceed along a predetermined route, accompanied by explanatory remarks from their keepers. The zoo characterised the event as a trial designed to assess visitor reactions before any permanent arrangement is adopted.
Demand clearly outstripped supply. Social media posts indicated that some visitors had queued from 8 a.m., and that by 9 a.m., the line extended as far as the Maokong Gondola station.

Crucially, the initiative serves a welfare function as well as a recreational one. Insufficient physical activity can predispose captive penguins to bumblefoot, a painful inflammation of the feet, so regular walks are regarded as a preventive measure.

Modelled on a well-established tradition at Asahiyama Zoo in Hokkaido, the Taipei parade will be confined to days when temperatures are below 24°C. To manage crowds within a confined space, the zoo may introduce numbered tickets, while visitors are expected to refrain from chasing, touching or feeding the birds.
sentZh: 台北市立動物園週四試辦的「企鵝遊行」吸引了出乎意料的大批觀眾，凸顯民眾對近距離接觸野生動物的熱衷。
在首場 15 分鐘的活動中，43 隻非洲企鵝獲准離開展區，沿著預先規劃的路線前進，飼育員則在旁說明。
動物園將這次活動定位為試辦，目的是在採取任何固定安排之前評估遊客的反應。
需求顯然遠超過供給。
社群媒體貼文顯示，有些遊客從早上 8 點就開始排隊，到了 9 點，隊伍已延伸到貓空纜車站。
關鍵在於，這項計畫除了休閒功能，也兼具動物福利的作用。
活動量不足可能使圈養企鵝容易罹患趾瘤症——一種疼痛的腳部發炎，因此定期散步被視為一種預防措施。
台北的遊行仿效北海道旭山動物園行之有年的傳統，將只在氣溫低於攝氏 24 度的日子舉行。
為了在有限空間內管理人潮，動物園可能實施號碼牌制度，同時要求遊客不要追逐、觸摸或餵食企鵝。
